rules.law_name: Measure BB amendments to Berkeley Rent Ordinance
rules.title: Measure BB rent-control and rent-increase changes
rules.requirement: For fully covered Berkeley rental units, annual rent increases remain tied to the Rent Ordinance CPI formula but the Annual General Adjustment cannot exceed 5%. Landlords of fully covered units may charge utilities only as part of base rent or through a separately metered utility account in the tenant’s name, and capital-improvement rent-increase petitions may be filed only for completed improvements.

coverage.other_unresolvable: Units where the tenant shares kitchen or bath facilities with the landlord are exempt only if the landlord lived in a unit on the same property at the start of the tenancy; subsidy-related coverage may depend on unit type and whether federal law, state law, or administrative regulation exempts the unit from rent control.
coverage.summary: Rent-control limits apply to fully covered units, described as most multifamily properties built before 1980, certain single-family home tenancies, certain room rentals, and some government-owned or subsidized units depending on legal restrictions.

rules.exemptions: Partially covered unit types include new construction units with a certificate of occupancy issued after 1980, most single-family homes, and most condominiums; certain subsidized units are only partially covered where federal law, state law, or administrative regulation prohibits rent control.
rules.interaction: The document states that federal law, state law, or administrative regulation may prohibit Berkeley rent control for certain subsidized units, making them partially rather than fully covered.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

rules.law_name: Measure BB amendments to Berkeley Rent Ordinance
rules.title: Measure BB just-cause eviction changes
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered Berkeley units may be evicted only for just cause; Measure BB bars nonpayment eviction unless the rental debt is at least one month of the applicable HUD Fair Market Rent, bars eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar fixed-term lease, and tightens material-lease-breach evictions. Termination notices must include Rent Board counseling information, and landlords must file copies of eviction notices and lawsuits with the Rent Board within three business days after service.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction requires rental debt equal to or greater than one month of Fair Market Rent; eviction documents due to Rent Board within 3 business days

coverage.other_unresolvable: Coverage depends on whether the unit is fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance; shared kitchen or bath units are exempt only if the landlord lived in a unit on the same property at the start of the tenancy, and subsidy-related coverage may depend on federal, state, or administrative rent-control restrictions.
coverage.summary: Just-cause eviction protections apply to tenants in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley’s Rent Ordinance.

rules.exemptions: Units exempt from the Berkeley Rent Ordinance are not described as covered by these just-cause protections; the document specifically notes a shared-kitchen-or-bath exemption only when the landlord lived on the same property at the start of the tenancy.
rules.interaction: The document describes the just-cause protections as part of Berkeley’s Rent Ordinance and notes that units may be fully covered, partially covered, or exempt under that ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”). Measure BB has changed some just causes, eliminated one just cause, added new requirements for eviction notices
